name: Python for AI Engineering
audience: Developers and architects who want fluent, idiomatic Python for data, ML and LLM applications. Basic programming experience assumed.
format: This site's course with a 40-question practice test mixing code-reading, debugging and design questions.
scenarios: Cleaning and analysing an eval dataset
verifyNotes: This is the site's own deep-foundations course, not a vendor certification: there are no exam facts to confirm, so spend Research on finding the best official/primary sources per topic (URLs that will be cited as sources) and on current library APIs. Goal: the learner should be able to explain and derive these ideas confidently in an interview or design review. Lessons go deep: intuition first, then the formal definition, then a fully worked numeric example, then exactly where it shows up in modern AI/LLMs, then a common misconception. Write math in LaTeX between double dollars only: $$...$$ (inline or on its own line for display); NEVER single-dollar math (single $ renders literally). In JSON strings escape backslashes (\\frac). Code in fenced ```python blocks that run as-is. Every lesson has a hands-on lab: a small Python exercise with the expected output. Question mix: ~40% concept/judgment, ~35% compute-or-predict (give numbers or code, ask for the result), ~25% debug-or-choose-the-right-approach. Verifiers MUST run every compute and code-output question with {{root}}/.pipeline/py/bin/python (Python 3.9 with NumPy 2.0, pandas 2.3, scikit-learn 1.6, PyTorch 2.8). Code that uses Python 3.10+ syntax (match, X | Y unions, 3.12 type-parameter syntax) cannot run there: label such items "(Python 3.10+)" in the stem and verify them by careful reasoning against docs.python.org and fix keys that disagree; state any randomness seed in the stem. Sources: official library docs and primary/canonical teaching material only (see src/content/official-domains.json, track "foundations"); no blogs or Medium. Target Python 3.12+ and current NumPy 2.x, pandas 2.x, PyTorch 2.x and scikit-learn APIs (no deprecated calls). For LLM API code, keep it provider-neutral or show the official SDK pattern of Anthropic, OpenAI or Google exactly as their docs show it; never invent SDK methods. Include implementing attention and a training loop from scratch in PyTorch.

domains.name: Python core and idioms
skills: Data model: mutability, identity vs equality, references, copying
Comprehensions, iterators, generators and itertools
Functions: closures, decorators, *args/**kwargs, keyword-only, default-argument pitfalls
Classes, dataclasses, protocols and type hints; Pydantic models for validated data
Exceptions, context managers, packaging and virtual environments (venv, pip, uv, pyproject.toml)

domains.name: NumPy and pandas for data work
skills: ndarray shapes, dtypes, views vs copies, indexing and boolean masks
Broadcasting rules and vectorisation instead of loops; einsum
Linear algebra in NumPy: matmul, norms, solving, SVD
pandas DataFrames: selection, groupby, merge/join, reshaping, missing data
Performance and memory: dtypes, chunking, avoiding chained assignment

domains.name: Machine learning with scikit-learn and PyTorch
skills: scikit-learn workflow: train/test split, pipelines, cross-validation, leakage, metrics
PyTorch tensors, devices, autograd and computational graphs
nn.Module, losses, optimisers and a correct training loop (zero_grad, backward, step, eval mode, no_grad)
Datasets and DataLoaders, batching and padding
Implementing embeddings, scaled dot-product attention and a tiny transformer block from scratch

domains.name: Building LLM applications in Python
skills: HTTP and official SDK clients, API keys from the environment, timeouts
async/await with asyncio: concurrency limits (Semaphore), gather, cancellation
Streaming responses, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, rate limits
Structured output with JSON Schema/Pydantic; tool-calling loops
Embeddings, cosine similarity search and a minimal RAG pipeline

domains.name: Testing, performance and reproducibility
skills: pytest: fixtures, parametrize, mocking external APIs
Logging and debugging (pdb, tracebacks)
Profiling; the GIL, threads vs processes vs asyncio
Reproducibility: seeds, pinned dependencies, deterministic evals
Notebook-to-module hygiene
